what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to authorize tax title foreclosure of 531 Reservoir Road and its eventual sale.
The board voted unanimously to entrust the remaining ARPA funds to the interim town manager, pending the school bid opening, with a report back.
The Budget Task Force gave a long joint presentation of recommendations on revenue and savings, including CPA and overrides; it was informational and no vote was taken.
The board heard the unaudited FY24 year-end financials, in which revenue came in above projection and free cash above the earlier estimate.
Town manager finalist interviews were set for January 14, with January 15 as backup, and the public may send candidate questions to the chair.

why_it_matters: The ARPA delegation means the last of the federal relief money can be committed by the interim town manager without a further board vote, with only a report back required.

The Budget Task Force's ideas on CPA and overrides are the kind of revenue options that would eventually reach residents as tax-bill changes or ballot questions, but nothing was decided at this meeting.
Foreclosure on the tax-title parcel moves it toward sale, and the choice of a permanent town manager will shape the next budget cycle.
watch_next: Town manager finalist interviews on January 14, with January 15 as backup.
The comparison communities list returning with an added wealth/affordability factor, followed by a formal vote.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to approve its skate park letter of support, with modifications noted.
The board voted unanimously to vacate a tax-lien foreclosure judgment on one Sunset Avenue property, subject to full redemption payment within 14 days.
The board put off deciding whether to retain or sell two foreclosed parcels under the new state law until next week, pending property cards and photos.
The board renewed the 2025 alcohol, auto dealer, common victualer and limousine licenses, each by unanimous vote.
The finance director's year-end report was postponed to next week, and a vote on the remaining ARPA contingency was deferred.

why_it_matters: Whether the town keeps or sells foreclosed parcels under the new state law decides if they return to private hands and the tax rolls or stay town property, and that vote is still ahead.
The ARPA contingency vote and the finance director's year-end report were both pushed back, so residents have not yet seen the closing figures or the use of the remaining federal funds.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board meeting: the retain-or-sell decision on 531 Reservoir Road and 56 Carr Avenue, the remaining ARPA contingency vote, and the finance director's year-end report.

meetings.headline: Select Board adopted a single tax rate with no exemptions, and committed ARPA funds to small local requests.
meetings.summary: The board held the FY2025 tax classification hearing. It heard the assessors' recommendation, took public comment, and voted for a single rate with no exemptions. It also approved a T-ball field agreement, a skate park grant support letter, an Agricultural Commission appointment, an ARPA reallocation and small ARPA grants, and a purchasing card policy. The interim town manager's report covered projects, recruitment and health insurance, and the board discussed cannabis host agreements and the special town meeting debrief.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to adopt a single tax rate and not adopt any available exemptions, following the assessors' recommendation.
After a public hearing with comment for and against a split rate, the board held no further delay; one speaker had asked for a one-week hold.
The board voted to change the Marshall Park ARPA allocation to the remaining amount, then committed ARPA funds to Boys and Girls Club equipment, Historical Society items and fencing.
The board approved t-ball use of the old primary school property, a skate park grant support letter, an Agricultural Commission appointment, and a purchasing card policy.
The interim town manager reported a two-year property insurance renewal and said health insurance renewals are expected in mid-January with a high trend rate.

why_it_matters: The single-rate vote means residential and commercial property are taxed at the same rate in the FY2025 tax bills, so no shift of the levy onto commercial property is built into the average single-family bill.
The ARPA votes reallocate a fixed, one-time pool of federal money, so each dollar committed to a small request is no longer available for other projects.
Health insurance is a large, recurring cost in the town budget, and a high renewal trend would press on the FY2026 budget the board will be asked to set.
watch_next: Health insurance renewal figures, expected in mid-January.
The skate park support letter, due back at the next meeting with a December 31 grant deadline; the climate survey policy and goal-setting are postponed to December.

what_happened.line: The Select Board extended the interim town manager's contract by 90 days on a 3-2 vote.
The board accepted Article 10, a salary plan change, with the manager's starting step capped at step four, then recommended it 3-1-1.
Article 2, an FY25 school budget amendment, was accepted and recommended unanimously; added Chapter 70 funds go to the school salary reserves line.
The board deferred its recommendation on Article 12 (Marshall Park debt) and on Article 13, a citizens petition, both unanimously.
A legacy budget amendment was added as new article one, then deferred; the warrant goes to the printer after proofing.

why_it_matters: The special town meeting warrant sets what residents will be asked to vote on, including salary plan changes for employees, a school budget amendment, and Marshall Park debt.
Recommendations on Articles 6, 12, 13 and the new legacy article are still open, so the board's position on them is not yet known to voters.
The interim manager arrangement now runs 90 more days, so the town's permanent manager search stays unsettled over that period.
watch_next: The special town meeting vote on the warrant, including Articles 10 and 11 and the deferred Articles 6, 12 and 13.
The board's recommendations on the deferred articles and the new legacy budget amendment article, once the manager updates the dates and the warrant is proofed.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to assign ARPA funds for a recruiting firm for the town manager screening committee and to request a reserve fund transfer for the same.
The board voted unanimously to approve the interim town manager contract discussed in executive session, contingent on labor counsel review.
The board approved additional hours for the recreation director, paid from the parks revolving account, and approved a sewer intermunicipal agreement with Leominster, both unanimously.
A dispute over whether last week's public communications policy vote was valid ended with no resolution and was deferred to a meeting with the full board present.
The Chapter 61B Kilburn Street hearing was continued to August 6, with the open space committee to be asked for input.

why_it_matters: The search for a new town manager is being paid for from ARPA money and possibly the reserve fund, so residents will see the same cost appear in a Finance Committee transfer request.
Whether the public communications policy is in effect is still contested, which affects how residents' comments and records requests are handled until town counsel weighs in.
The Kilburn Street Chapter 61B decision is still open, and it concerns land the town may have a right to consider buying.
watch_next: August 6: the continued Chapter 61B Kilburn Street hearing, with the applicant on the agenda.
The Finance Committee's action on the reserve fund transfer request for the recruiter, and town counsel's answer on the communications policy.

meetings.headline: Select Board interviewed two interim Town Manager candidates and chose Mr. terenzini first, Blanchard second, unanimously.
meetings.summary: The board interviewed two candidates for interim Town Manager, Charlie Blanchard and Carter terenzini, asking the same questions about availability, budgets, town meeting, hiring and management style. In discussion, members agreed both were qualified, and all leaned to terenzini partly because he has no stated hour limit. They split up reference checks, asked the Town Council-side staff to draft an agreement and get salary ranges, and voted a first and second choice before adjourning.

meetings.headline: Select Board adopted a public communications policy 3-2 after one night's notice, and took no action on the Flat Hill Road petition.

The board ratified the Building Commissioner / land use manager appointment and approved the town manager's slate of annual appointments.

A proposed budget task force was tabled for more work on its makeup and charge, to be drafted using another town's as a model.

why_it_matters: The town is choosing who will run Lunenburg day to day on an interim basis, and the screening process set here shapes who the board sees.

Leftover ARPA money is one-time funding, and how the board sorts committed from uncommitted decides which small projects residents raised, such as the DPW garage and the Council on Aging lot, can still be paid for.
A budget task force, once its charge is settled, would shape how future budgets are built and presented to voters.

why_it_matters: Writing off ambulance receivables removes old billed amounts the town was carrying as owed, so it bears on how much ambulance revenue the town can count on collecting.

The revenue turnover policy, which sets how revenue is handled, is still undecided, and other boards will see it before the Select Board votes.
watch_next: The revenue turnover policy returns at the Select Board's next meeting, one week out.
The town meeting consent calendar, as drafted, goes to the floor with no articles pulled.

what_happened.line: The Select Board amended the school override article, article H, to carry a stated dollar amount and placed it on the town meeting warrant.
The board placed articles A through Z on the warrant, then recommended approval of articles A, B, C, I, L, M, N, P, T and W, each 5-0.
The board deferred its recommendation on articles Y and Z to town meeting, and put articles still lacking numbers over to next week.
The town manager reported that new positions were pulled from the budget to cover a possible trash contract increase and wage impacts, with the final gap closed by raising local receipts estimates.
The school committee will send its final override number after its Wednesday meeting so the board can modify article H next week.

why_it_matters: The school override is headed to a ballot question, so residents will be asked to vote on a Proposition 2 1/2 amount that is still open to change next week.

The trash contract, which the hauler indicated would rise sharply to extend, and the removal of new positions bear on town services and on how much of the budget gap is met by estimates rather than cuts.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board meeting: the final override number from the school committee, the override ballot wording and recommendation, and a public hearing on early voting by mail.
The deferred warrant articles that still have no numbers, and the board's decision on adding to article V after hearing from the board of assessors.

meetings.headline: Select Board agreed to reallocate ARPA funds to the schools to narrow the budget gap; override vote deferred to March 26.
meetings.summary: The board held joint and scheduled appointments, heard a water district PFAS update, a conservation staffing plan, and a town manager report including a large trash contract increase. The main item was reallocating ARPA money to the school budget to close most of the gap to the school committee's minimum budget, with debate over whether the override still goes on the warrant and ballot. Warrant articles were reviewed, a late citizen petition was ruled not actionable, and an early-voting question was deferred pending a posted public hearing.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted by roll call to move sidewalk ARPA money to the school department, plus more uncommitted ARPA money for 911, network security and Chromebooks.
The town manager proposed pausing the pavement management plan for a year and redirecting those funds to the schools; with ARPA, the schools get close to, not fully to, the minimum budget.
A decision on the override was deferred; the board set a special meeting on the override and warrant for March 26 at 7 pm.
The town manager reported that extending the trash hauler contract on current terms would bring a large increase, so the town requested a 90-day extension and will go out to bid.
A late, unsigned citizen petition to add department funding to the override was ruled not actionable, and warrant article recommendations were deferred.

why_it_matters: Moving one-time ARPA money and paving funds to the school budget narrows the gap without a tax increase, but does not close it, so residents may still be asked to vote on an override.
The trash contract will be rebid after the 90-day extension, and the larger price at the new contract could change what the town spends on solid waste and recycling next year.

Public hearing on early in-person voting, posted for April 2; assessors and Council on Aging revised senior exemption article due April 2.

The board accepted the warrant article lowering the low-income senior exemption age and sent it to Town Counsel to modify the language.
The board suspended its 60-day notice policy for ballot questions, so override language can be finalized later.
The school override placeholder stays on the warrant, with a special meeting targeted for March 26 to settle the language and the number.
The school committee's override request was described as a little over a million dollars, with the number still moving.

why_it_matters: The single tax rate means residential and commercial property are taxed at the same rate, which sets how the levy is split among tax bills.
The school override is a question residents will be asked to vote on, and its wording and size are not yet fixed.
Lowering the senior exemption age would widen who qualifies for a tax break, with the cost absorbed within the town's overlay account.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved Conrad's Drive-In license on condition that back taxes are resolved or a payment plan is in place by May 20th.

The town manager's budget inputs (health insurance, electricity, Monty Tech, FEMA storm reimbursement) feed the coming budget and the Proposition 2½ levy picture residents will vote on.

what_happened.line: The Select Board appointed Jenny puther to the Conservation Commission by roll call, for a term expiring June 30, 2024.
The town manager reported the town lost its mid-year 40R smart growth reimbursement because the calculation came out negative, and does not plan to budget it next year.
The board debated the chapter 74 bylaw repeal at length and did not vote; it will return to the item on Feb. 13.
Members discussed FY25 budget inputs and an override; health insurance, Monty Tech and Worcester County Retirement numbers are still outstanding.
The chair invited the state delegation and the school and finance committee chairs to meet on Feb. 20 about Prop 2.5 and 40R funding.

why_it_matters: The lost 40R aid is a revenue shortfall the town manager expects local receipts to cover at year-end close, so it bears on how much room the FY25 budget has under the Proposition 2.5 levy limit.
With several FY25 cost inputs still outstanding and the override discussion unresolved, residents cannot yet tell whether a tax-bill question will reach a town vote this year.
The chapter 74 bylaw repeal is still undecided, so a bylaw change could come back for a vote on Feb. 13.

what_happened.line: The Select Board denied a request for a financial audit of the police department; no member wanted to pursue it.
The board gave the town manager guidance to keep replies to one resident's repeated complaints brief and to invite him to appear before the board.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of a facilities superintendent and approved a Class 2 auto dealer license, 4-0 by roll call.
The board opened the annual town meeting warrant on January 9 and set it to close March 18, 2024 at 4 p.m., 4-0 by roll call.
A member reported the superintendent presented a worst-case scenario of cutting school and central office positions, partly tied to the end of ESSER money.

why_it_matters: The school position cuts, a health insurance increase still to be set, and electricity rates going to bid in spring are early pressures on the budgets residents will vote on at town meeting.
The warrant closes March 18, 2024, which is the deadline for articles to be placed before voters at the annual town meeting.
watch_next: The town meeting warrant closes March 18, 2024 at 4 p.m.
Next week's board agenda: town manager goals update, ARPA update and the draft board committee handbook.
